commitResults.messageTitle: Reject the retired address prefix explicitly
commitResults.messageBody:
The add and edit tokenizers do not recognise a/, so it was folded into the preceding value and reported as an invalid email, date, amount or venue. Reject a/ at the command boundary for prefix-based commands before field validation.

Keep free text such as s/o, c/o and n/a valid, and leave find untouched because it accepts arbitrary search text. Document the retired prefix and add regression tests for the original command and legitimate slash-bearing values.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject mistyped prefixes with a clear diagnostic
commitResults.messageBody:
Unknown prefixes are currently folded into the preceding value. For
example, sub/ in add is parsed as part of the name, and a/ after an
email is blamed on the email, so users are told the wrong field is
malformed. A prefix from another command is also only reported
indirectly as a missing parameter.

Let's compare unaccepted prefix-shaped tokens with the command's
accepted prefixes and likely parameter names in ArgumentMultimap. Run
this check before required-prefix, duplicate and value checks, keep
notes, feedback, reasons and remarks permissive, and preserve c/o, d/o,
s/o, n/a and w/o as ordinary text.

The shared check keeps command-specific parsers small and makes the
diagnostic consistent across student, lesson, homework, task and finance
commands. Add exhaustive regression cases and document the user-visible
behaviour.

commitResults.messageTitle: Harden prefix diagnostics across text fields
commitResults.messageBody:
Descriptions currently treat every slash-bearing token as prose, so a
field name such as name/ is absorbed and the parser reports an
unrelated missing parameter. The retired a/ prefix follows the same
path in descriptions, losing its venue hint. Archive and sort also
bypass the shared check because they have no tokenized parameters.

Let's apply the existing description rules in homework and task
commands, let the shared multimap detect a/ before prose exemptions
outside fully permissive fields, and run the check from archive and
sort. Extend the regression cases to cover these fields and the
cross-command matrix while keeping quoted commands in notes, feedback,
reasons and remarks valid.

commitResults.messageTitle: Restore retired-prefix checks for index subcommands
commitResults.messageBody:
Removing the command-boundary check also removed the a/ venue hint from
index-only paths such as pay reverse, hw delete, task done and lesson
missed. Those paths do not tokenize prefixes, so the shared multimap
check cannot see the retired token.

Let's apply the retired-prefix diagnostic to the non-prefix subcommands
that previously had it, while leaving free text in notes, feedback,
reasons and remarks permissive.

Check repeated lesson-repeat prefixes before missing required fields so
a replacement typo reports the duplicate prefix that actually caused
it. Document the restored path and add regression coverage for
mixed-case command words.

logic, UI, payment, today and delete diagrams in line with the current
